facts.t: The American Constitution mentions only one emergency power
facts.d: The suspension of habeas corpus in cases of rebellion or invasion. Everything else — the National Emergencies Act, the Stafford Act, IEEPA — is statute Congress wrote and can repeal, not constitutional text.

facts.t: Washington cannot dismiss a state government
facts.d: There is no American equivalent of Article 356. Even at the height of a declared national emergency, a state governor and legislature stay in office. India's President's Rule has no counterpart in any comparable federation.

facts.t: The steel seizure case still sets the limit
facts.d: In Youngstown Sheet and Tube (1952) the Supreme Court blocked President Truman from seizing steel mills during the Korean War. Justice Jackson's concurrence — grading presidential power by whether Congress has authorised, is silent, or has forbidden — remains the governing framework.

bank.q: Comparing emergency regimes, consider the following statements:
s: India codifies emergency powers expressly in Part XVIII.
The United States has a consolidated constitutional emergency code.
American emergency powers flow mainly from statutes such as the National Emergencies Act.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The United States has no consolidated code — only the habeas corpus suspension clause is express.

bank.q: The only emergency power expressly written into the United States Constitution concerns:
o: Suspension of habeas corpus in rebellion or invasion
Suspension of the Bill of Rights
bank.e: The Suspension Clause. Every other emergency authority is statutory.

bank.q: Which one of the following does NOT follow from an American emergency declaration?
o: Activation of statutory powers Congress has granted
Congressional review under the National Emergencies Act
Dismissal of a state government by the federal executive
Judicial review of the President's claimed authority
bank.e: The federal government cannot dismiss a state government — there is no equivalent of Article 356.

bank.as: India's emergency design is described as centralising and America's as decentralised.
bank.rs: An Indian proclamation shifts authority over states, rights and finances to the Union, whereas an American declaration does not transform federalism.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the structural difference, not merely a difference in degree.

bank.q: Match List I (provision or instrument) with List II (effect):
pairs: 1. Congressional review and termination by joint resolution
2. Automatic suspension of Article 19 in war or external aggression
3. Presidential emergency claims limited absent authorisation
4. Suspension of enforcement of specified Fundamental Rights
bank.e: Article 358 suspends Article 19 automatically in external-aggression emergencies; Article 359 suspends enforcement of specified rights; the NEA supplies congressional control; Youngstown supplies the judicial limit.

bank.q: With reference to rights during emergency, consider the following statements:
s: Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended in India.
American constitutional rights are not automatically suspended by a declaration.
Article 358 applies whether the emergency arises from external aggression or armed rebellion.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. After the 44th Amendment, Article 358's automatic suspension of Article 19 applies only where the ground is war or external aggression.

bank.q: Which requirement was introduced by the 44th Amendment before a National Emergency may be proclaimed?
o: Prior approval of the Rajya Sabha
A written recommendation of the Union Cabinet
A report from the Chief Justice of India
bank.e: The Union Cabinet's recommendation must be in writing — a direct response to the 1975 proclamation, which had been advised by the Prime Minister alone.

bank.q: All of the following describe the underlying philosophy of the two systems EXCEPT:
o: India's Constitution anticipates breakdowns and provides for national survival
The American Constitution distrusts undefined executive power
American emergency power requires congressional authorisation
India requires state ratification before an emergency takes effect
bank.e: No state ratification is involved. Indian emergencies require parliamentary approval, not state consent.

bank.q: Parliamentary approval of a proclamation under Article 352 requires:
o: A simple majority in both Houses
A special majority in both Houses
A simple majority in the Lok Sabha alone
Ratification by half the state legislatures
bank.e: A special majority. President's Rule under Article 356, by contrast, needs only a simple majority.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about judicial control of emergency powers:
s: S. R. Bommai made proclamations under Article 356 judicially reviewable.
Youngstown limited presidential emergency claims lacking constitutional or congressional authority.
Indian courts may review the adequacy of the reasons underlying a proclamation.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Indian review extends to mala fides and irrelevant grounds, not to the sufficiency of the reasons.
